correctness.rationale: For each hub-free coalition R the payoff 2e_H(R)/|R|≤|R|/2, equality only at an edge; degree≤2 and excluded short cycles yield the strict larger cases. Hub block {h}∪S contributes 2(|S|+e_H(S))/(|S|+1)≤1+|S|/2 with equality only at edge (s=2) or induced P3 (s=3). Equality forces a perfect matching of the remaining vertices. Casewise deviation payoff bounds show the hub and all paired or selected vertices cannot strictly gain by unilateral moves, including joining singleton or any other coalition. Independent exhaustive partition/matching/stability checks passed for four fans and five wheels, with orientation-normalized cycle edges. Infinite family proof is the local edge bounds, not enumeration.

value.rationale: A sharp, efficiently certifiable welfare-bound attainment criterion and exact enumeration/stability for an infinite graph family are motivated optimization facts; distinguishing when price of Nash stability is one avoids an unmotivated tiny-instance census.

final_claim: For apex graphs K1∨H where H is finite degree≤2 and has no 3- or 4-cycles, sharp welfare SW≤m/2+1 is attained iff a hub-plus-edge or hub-plus-P3 motif leaves a perfectly matchable H; all attaining partitions are Nash stable and counted by two perfect-matching deletion sums. Fans and long wheels have explicit optimum counts, short wheels are separately classified.
limitations: The theorem characterizes attainment of a sharp upper bound, not exact optimum below bound when no matching certificate; excludes short cycles in H and nonbinary weights.
residual_risks: The exact matching-certificate and Nash characterization might occur as a special case in a broader unindexed hedonic optimization theorem.
